conventions.convention: The quaternionic coordinate map is j(λ₁,λ₂,μ₁,μ₂)=(-conj(λ₂),conj(λ₁),-conj(μ₂),conj(μ₁)); j²=-1 and σ([z])=[jz]. Real twistor lines are projectivizations of j-invariant complex two-planes, including the infinity line λ₁=λ₂=0.
Sigma-Hermitian pairings are linear in the first slot. The line-section form evaluates h at s(x) and the conjugate of t(σx), and positivity concerns this constant line-section form.
For homogeneous linear matrices, P#(z)=P(jz)†. The signed dual monad has differentials -β# and α#, with (P#)#=-P and D²(M)=M.
The raw moments are μC=[B₁,B₂]+IJ and μR=[B₁,B₁†]+[B₂,B₂†]+II†-J†J. Stability is the word-span condition; costability excludes nonzero common invariant subspaces in ker J.

First-order coefficients lie in A=C[ε]/(ε²), with conjugation fixing ε. Positivity is imposed only after reduction. The family range requires the stated free global-section module, direct-summand coefficient image, and fixed-real-line triviality and section base change. Allowed base maps are reduction and ε↦rε for real r.

Htop=c₁(O(1)) is the dual-tautological hyperplane class. With z₁=x⁰+ix¹ and z₂=x²+ix³, the base orientation is dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³ and fibers have complex orientation; π*u=Htop². The conclusion c₂(E)=ku requires the topological pullback hypothesis F≅π*E.

load_bearing.statement: For the coefficient-image subspace of the reduced linear monad, with no global sections, trivial positive real-line restrictions, nondegenerate Hermitian H, β(z)=α(jz)†H and βα=0, H is positive definite on the entire coefficient-image subspace.

For locally split linear monads on P³ with locally free middle cohomology and the stated analytic O, O(-1), and O(-2) cohomology hypotheses, every holomorphic morphism of middle cohomology bundles lifts to a unique constant chain map. A nondegenerate sigma-Hermitian self-pairing lifts to a chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle map H and normalized identities β(z)=α(jz)†H and β(jz)†=-Hα(z).

Under the stated locally split monad, Hermitian-duality, scalar-cohomology and positive real-line section-form hypotheses, H⁰(F)=L=M⊥, H restricted to L is positive definite, and S=L⊕M orthogonally. The constant summand splits off, while the reduced cohomology has no global sections and remains positive on every real line.

Assume full AC. Analytic sheaf cohomology of O(-1) vanishes in every degree on Pʳ for 1≤r≤3, and that of O(-2) vanishes in every degree for r=2,3. These are analytic deductions from scalar cohomology and hyperplane sequences, without GAGA.

For N≥1, k≥0 and complex ADHM data satisfying [B₁,B₂]+IJ=0, a_z is injective for every z exactly when the datum is costable, and b_z† is surjective for every z exactly when it is stable. Full homogeneous ranks imply regularity; regularity together with both zero moments gives the displayed homogeneous bundle monad.

Assume full AC, k≥0 and N≥2. A locally split holomorphic monad of dimensions (k,2k+N,k), with locally free cohomology trivial on the finite real twistor lines, positive nondegenerate sigma-Hermitian pairing and unitary infinity framing, admits the displayed raw regular zero-moment ADHM normal form. Conversely every such regular zero-moment datum gives this monad structure. Normalized framed isomorphisms correspond exactly to U(V). The theorem also states the explicit compact-torus chain factors and the first-order classification only in its specified locally-free/base-change range.

For k,N≥0 and locally free algebraic middle cohomology of the exact-ended monad O(-1)^k→O^(2k+N)→O(1)^k on P³, ch(F)=N-kHalg², c₁alg(F)=0, c₂alg(F)=kHalg² and χ(F)=N-2k. Analytification has total topological Chern class 1+kHtop² through degree six. In the stated positive twistor orientation π*u=Htop²; if the underlying topological bundle is π*E with c₁(E)=0, then c₂(E)=ku.
